security_audit.summary: All 11 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around flags, a file path, a documented command, and a naming pattern. No prompt injection, reconnaissance, or executable Ruby or shell backtick behavior appears in SKILL.md. A medium-risk concern remains because the workflow can lead agents toward remote repository mutations without a mandatory confirmation gate.

remediation.issue: Remote repository actions do not have a mandatory confirmation gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before pushes, direct main changes, pull request creation, auto-merge, reviewer assignments, or metadata updates. Default to dry-run behavior.

content.user_title: Orchestrate Git and Pull Request Workflows
content.value_statement: Complex Git changes can reach review without consistent testing, commit structure, or deployment checks. This skill organizes review, validation, commits, branches, and pull request preparation.
actual_capabilities: Coordinates staged code review, dependency analysis, testing, commit planning, branch preparation, and pull request creation.
Requests severity-ranked code review findings and breaking-change assessments from specialized agents.
Plans unit, integration, and end-to-end test execution with coverage and gap analysis.
Generates Conventional Commit messages and recommends atomic commit structure.
Prepares branch strategies, pre-push checks, pull request descriptions, metadata, and reviewer checklists.
Provides success criteria and rollback steps for changes after merge.
limitations: Depends on specialized agent types that may not exist in every host environment.
References a detailed playbook that is not included in the published file set.
Does not define executable automation, so agents must translate guidance into repository-specific commands.
Cannot guarantee test coverage, branch protection, reviewer availability, or deployment readiness.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature Pull Request
use_cases.description: A software developer uses staged reviews, tests, commit guidance, and branch checks before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Reviews
use_cases.description: A repository maintainer applies consistent quality, security, compatibility, and reviewer checks across incoming changes.

use_cases.title: Assess Release Readiness
use_cases.description: A release engineer combines test results, breaking-change analysis, branch policy, and rollback planning before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Review Changes Before a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my uncommitted changes for a pull request targeting [branch]. Identify quality issues, missing tests, and breaking changes. Do not modify files or push.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Conventional Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Conventional Commit plan for [change summary]. Recommend atomic commits, scopes, subjects, and any breaking-change footer after reviewing the current diff.

prompt_templates.title: Run Staged Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the staged validation workflow for [target branch]. Review changes, execute available tests, report coverage gaps, verify branch readiness, and stop before remote actions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Draft Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a draft pull request for [change]. Include review findings, test evidence, migration needs, deployment notes, rollback steps, labels, and reviewer recommendations. Request approval before any remote action.

output_examples.input: Review a payment retry change before opening a pull request.
output: Review summary: one high-risk duplicate-charge path requires resolution.
Testing: unit coverage exists, but an integration test for repeated timeouts is missing.
Recommendation: block the pull request until retry idempotency and integration coverage are verified.

output_examples.input: Plan commits for an authentication timeout fix and related tests.
output: Recommended structure: one fix commit for timeout handling and one test commit for regression coverage.
Breaking change: none identified from the supplied change summary.

output_examples.input: Prepare a draft pull request summary for a database migration.
output: Summary: adds the migration and preserves compatibility during deployment.
Validation: migration tests pass, while rollback timing still needs staging verification.
Deployment note: apply the migration before enabling dependent application behavior.

best_practices: Confirm the target branch, repository policies, and remote action permissions before starting.
Resolve critical and high-severity findings before creating commits or pull requests.
Preserve test evidence, breaking-change notes, and rollback details in the pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not skip tests without documenting the reason and residual risk.
Do not push, rewrite history, enable auto-merge, or modify remote metadata without explicit approval.
Do not claim coverage, CI readiness, or branch protection compliance without verified results.

faq.question: Does this skill create pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide or coordinate pull request creation. Remote actions depend on available tools and should require explicit approval.

faq.question: Which development strategies does it support?
faq.answer: It covers feature-branch and trunk-based workflows, with configurable draft, squash, conventional commit, test, and no-push options.

faq.question: Does it execute tests?
faq.answer: It instructs a testing agent to run available suites and report coverage. Results depend on the repository and host environment.

faq.question: Can it generate commit messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It categorizes changes and prepares Conventional Commit messages, including scopes, rationale, issue references, and breaking-change notes.

faq.question: Does the skill modify repository files?
faq.answer: The skill contains instructions rather than scripts. Authorized host agents may execute repository commands while following the workflow.

faq.question: Is the referenced implementation playbook included?
faq.answer: No. The published file structure contains only SKILL.md, so the referenced playbook is unavailable.
